summary: Naphazoline is an imidazoline alpha-adrenergic agonist used topically as an ocular and nasal decongestant. Ophthalmic drops relieve redness from minor eye irritation; instill 1-2 drops in the affected eye up to 4 times daily. Overuse causes rebound redness (and rebound nasal congestion for nasal forms). It should be avoided in narrow-angle glaucoma and used cautiously in young children, in whom systemic absorption can cause CNS and cardiovascular depression.
indications: Temporary relief of redness of the eye due to minor irritation (ophthalmic)
Relief of dryness and minor irritation of the eye (ophthalmic, with lubricant)
Temporary relief of nasal congestion (nasal formulations)

dosage.d: Instill 1-2 drops in the affected eye(s) up to 4 times daily
dosage.n: Do not use longer than 72 hours without medical advice

dosage.d: 1-2 sprays/drops per nostril every 6 hours as needed
dosage.n: Limit to 3-5 days to avoid rebound congestion

admin: Do not touch the dropper or spray tip to any surface to avoid contamination
Replace the cap after use; do not use if the solution changes color or becomes cloudy
Remove soft contact lenses before instilling eye drops
Do not use beyond 72 hours (eye) or 3-5 days (nose) without medical advice
moa: Naphazoline is an imidazoline sympathomimetic that stimulates alpha-adrenergic receptors on arterioles of the conjunctiva or nasal mucosa, producing vasoconstriction. This reduces blood-vessel engorgement, decreasing redness (eye) and mucosal swelling/congestion (nose). It has little or no beta-adrenergic activity.

relative: Infants and young children (systemic CNS/CV depression risk)

preg: Limited data. Systemic absorption from topical use is low; use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and for the shortest time.
lact: Limited data on excretion in breast milk. Systemic exposure from topical use is low; use with caution and avoid prolonged use while breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment for topical use; systemic absorption is minimal.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment for topical use; systemic absorption is minimal.

major: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors - risk of hypertensive reaction if significant systemic absorption occurs
moderate: Tricyclic antidepressants and other sympathomimetics - potentiated pressor effects
interactions.diagnostics: Causes conjunctival blanching/vasoconstriction and may transiently dilate pupils, which can interfere with ophthalmic examination.

common: Transient stinging or burning of the eye
Rebound redness (eye) or rebound congestion (nose) with overuse
serious: Increased intraocular pressure / angle-closure attack in susceptible eyes
Systemic CNS and cardiovascular depression in infants/children (hypothermia, bradycardia, somnolence)
rare: Hypertension, tachycardia or arrhythmia from systemic absorption
emergency: Severe CNS/cardiovascular depression after ingestion (especially in children)

monitoring: Duration of use - watch for rebound redness or congestion
Symptoms of eye pain, persistent redness or worsening over 72 hours
Blood pressure in patients with cardiovascular disease
counsel: Use the eye drops only for short-term redness relief, not beyond 3 days without advice
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or any surface
Overuse can make redness worse (rebound) - use sparingly
Stop and see a doctor if you have eye pain, vision changes or redness lasting over 72 hours
Keep out of reach of children; if swallowed, contact a poison center immediately
pk: Not well characterized for topical use
Decongestant/redness relief lasts a few hours
Store at room temperature; do not use if discolored or cloudy
pearls: Rebound redness/congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa for nasal use) limits use to a few days
Ingestion in infants/children can cause serious CNS and cardiovascular depression - keep out of reach
Use cautiously with MAO inhibitors and in cardiovascular disease
Remove soft contact lenses before instilling ophthalmic drops
missed: Naphazoline is used as needed for symptom relief rather than on a fixed schedule, so there is no missed-dose concern. Do not use more frequently than directed to avoid rebound symptoms.
overdose: Topical overuse causes rebound redness/congestion. Systemic overdose or ingestion (highest risk in children) can cause CNS depression, drowsiness, hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension and, paradoxically, hypertension. Treatment is supportive; contact a poison control center.
